findings.title: Mass Exploitation of (Un)authenticated Zimbra RCE: CVE-2022-27925
findings.summary_md: Volexity reported mass exploitation of CVE-2022-27925, an mboximport RCE in Zimbra Collaboration Suite, enabled as unauthenticated by the CVE-2022-37042 authentication bypass, with evidence of attacks as early as the end of June 2022. Internet-wide scanning identified over 1,000 backdoored ZCS instances worldwide, including government departments, ministries, and military branches. The post documents POST requests to /service/extension/backup/mboximport returning 401 as an exploitation signature, provides YARA rules for the deployed webshells, and lists patches 8.8.15P31/P33 and 9.0.0P24/P26.

findings.title: Russian State-Sponsored Actors Exploiting Zimbra... (AA22-228A)
findings.summary_md: Joint CISA and MS-ISAC advisory, initial version August 16, 2022, responding to active exploitation of multiple ZCS vulnerabilities: CVE-2022-24682, CVE-2022-27924, CVE-2022-27925 chained with CVE-2022-37042, and CVE-2022-30333. It warns that unpatched or internet-exposed ZCS instances in government and private sector networks should be assumed compromised and provides Snort signatures, IOCs, and detection guidance for hunting.

findings.title: Zimbra Collaboration Kepler 9.0.0 Patch 41 GA Release
findings.summary_md: Vendor patch release dated September 4, 2024 fixing CVE-2024-45519, a vulnerability in the postjournal service that may allow unauthenticated users to execute commands, rated CVSS 9.8. Zimbra's security advisories table maps the same fix to 10.0.9, 10.1.1, and 8.8.15 Patch 46, crediting researcher lebr0nli (Alan Li).

findings.title: Security vulnerability discovered in the postjournal service of Zimbra Collaboration Suite
findings.summary_md: Kudelski Security's advisory for CVE-2024-45519 describes an unauthenticated RCE in the postjournal email processing module, exploitable by sending a specially crafted email to a vulnerable server, affecting 8.8.15 up to Patch 45 and 9.0.0 up to Patch 40. It recommends updating to 8.8.15 Patch 46, 9.0.0 Patch 41, 10.0.9, or 10.1.1, restricting or disabling the postjournal service as a workaround, and monitoring system logs for suspicious postjournal activity.

findings.title: Critical Zimbra Vulnerability Exploited One Day After PoC Release
findings.summary_md: Early exploitation coverage reporting that CVE-2024-45519, a critical-severity vulnerability in Zimbra, was exploited in the wild to deploy a web shell on vulnerable servers one day after a public proof-of-concept appeared.

findings.title: Hackers exploited Zimbra flaw as zero-day using iCalendar files
findings.summary_md: Bill Toulas reports StrikeReady research showing CVE-2025-27915 was exploited as a zero-day starting at the beginning of January 2025, before Zimbra shipped 9.0.0 Patch 44, 10.0.13, and 10.1.5 on January 27, 2025 without mentioning exploitation. The attack spoofed the Libyan Navy's Office of Protocol to hit a Brazilian military organization with a Base64-obfuscated JavaScript payload in an oversized .ICS attachment that stole credentials, email, and contacts, added a mail filter named Correo forwarding to a Proton address, and exfiltrated through the Zimbra SOAP API every four hours. TTP overlap with UNC1151 is noted, and Zimbra told the outlet the activity did not appear widespread.
